图注: Figure 1. Integrated transcriptomic analysis and differential expression in colorectal cancer. (A,B) PCA before and after ComBat correction. Each point represents a sample; colors and shapes distinguish datasets, and ellipses summarize their distributions. (C) Volcano plot for tumor versus normal tissue. Orange and blue indicate upregulated and downregulated genes, respectively; gray indicates genes not meeting both FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1. (D) Heatmap of 50 upregulated and 50 downregulated genes. Colors represent row Z-scores on a displayed scale from −3 to 3.

Figure 2. Integration of eQTL associations with differential expression. (A,B) Overlap between genes with an unadjusted IVW P < 0.05 and upregulated or downregulated genes. (C) IVW ORs and 95% CIs for the 12 overlapping genes. The dashed line indicates OR = 1. P values are unadjusted. Venn circle areas are schematic.

Figure 3. Integration of pQTL associations with differential expression. (A,B) Overlap between genes encoding proteins with an unadjusted IVW P < 0.05 and upregulated or downregulated genes. (C) IVW ORs and 95% CIs for the eight overlapping candidates. The dashed line indicates OR = 1. P values are unadjusted; GREM1 and HHIP passed the full-scan FDR threshold. Venn circle areas are schematic.

Figure 4. Functional enrichment and network-based prioritisation of candidate effector genes. A:GSEA of 12,990 genes ranked by tumour-versus-normal log2 fold change, showing the five most significant terms per GO category and KEGG (BH-adjusted P < 0.05). Position denotes the leading-edge gene fraction within each ranked gene set; point area and fill indicate leading-edge gene count and −log10(FDR), respectively. Line colours distinguish GO BP, CC, MF and KEGG. B–D: Degree, maximal clique centrality (MCC) and maximum neighbourhood component (MNC) scores calculated on the 36-node, 100-edge STRING network, with ranking restricted to 16 inner-ring CEGs. Top-10 selection retaining boundary ties yields 11, 10 and 16 CEGs, respectively, with 10 shared genes. Yellow-to-coral fills indicate increasing method-specific scores among selected CEGs; grey denotes unselected CEGs and blue-grey denotes the 20 outer-ring neighbours. Node sizes distinguish rings, not scores. CEG, candidate effector gene; GO BP/CC/MF, biological process/cellular component/molecular function.

Figure 5. Machine-learning-based reduction of candidate hub genes and evaluation of a three-gene panel. (A, B) LASSO coefficient paths and development-cohort cross-validation performance. Dashed lines indicate the lambda selected by the one-standard-error rule. (C) Inner-cross-validation AUCs for SVM-RFE across feature counts and C values. Shading denotes the specified three-to-five-gene range; the open marker denotes the selected model. (D) Gene-selection frequencies across 25 outer-training fits under the constrained strategy. Green bars identify the locked panel. (E) ROC curves for the locked one-gene and three-gene models in the previously evaluated GSE20916 cohort. (F) Confusion matrix for the three-gene model at a probability threshold of 0.5; percentages are calculated within each observed class.

Figure 6. Immune composition and its associations with three candidate genes in colorectal cancer. (A) CIBERSORT relative fractions in primary tumours (n = 102) and adjacent normal tissues (n = 12) passing the deconvolution P < 0.05 threshold. Boxes indicate medians and interquartile ranges; whiskers extend to 1.5 times the interquartile range, with outliers shown as points. Group comparisons use site-adjusted linear models with patient-clustered robust standard errors and BH correction across 22 cell types. (B) Lower-triangular heatmap of cell-fraction Spearman correlations within tumours, overlaid with gene–cell association links. Coloured links indicate FDR < 0.05: terracotta, positive; teal, negative. Grey links indicate nonsignificant associations. Coloured line width represents absolute rho. (C) Spearman correlations between the three genes and immune-cell fractions in tumours. Numbers show rho, and asterisks indicate BH-adjusted significance across 66 gene–cell tests: * FDR < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001; ns, not significant. DC, dendritic cells; Tfh, follicular helper T cells.

Figure 7. Single-cell localization of candidate genes and intercellular communication in colorectal cancer. (A) UMAP of GSE132465 cells coloured by published major cell type. (B–D) EPB41L3, KLB and ANGPTL1 expression. Blue-grey denotes zero expression; the shared warm-colour scale denotes positive log-normalized expression. All cells retain their original coordinates. (E) Expression by cell type in normal and tumour tissues; dot size indicates the fraction of cells with detectable expression and colour indicates mean log-normalized expression. UMAP panels use stratified visualization samples, whereas panel E includes all retained cells. (F,G) Tumour CellChat networks showing interaction counts and summed communication strengths. Node area indicates sampled cell number, edge colour denotes the sender, and edge width indicates interaction count (F) or strength (G). (H) Selected interactions from myofibroblasts, smooth-muscle cells and SPP1+ myeloid cells to the indicated myeloid, T-cell and epithelial populations. Twenty ligand–receptor pairs were selected by summed communication probability within these directions. Dot colour represents communication probability and size represents the permutation-P category; blank positions indicate interactions not retained at P<0.05. CellChat used 100 permutations. Panels A–E include both tissue classes; F–H show tumour communication.

Figure 8. Spatial expression, detection and autocorrelation of candidate genes in colorectal tumors. (A) Spatial expression of EPB41L3, KLB and ANGPTL1. Rows represent sections C1–C4; columns show the original H&E image and log-normalized gene expression. Gray spots indicate zero counts. Each gene uses a shared color scale across sections. Expression-panel H&E backgrounds were uniformly blended with white to 30% image intensity. Scale bars, 500 μm, calculated from deposited scaling factors and the standard 55-μm Visium spot diameter. Retained spot counts were 2,054, 3,077, 3,330 and 3,969, respectively. (B) Dot size and color indicate the percentage of spots with detectable expression. (C) Moran’s I for each gene and section; asterisks indicate Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted permutation P < 0.05 across 12 tests, with 999 permutations per test.

Figure 9. RCTD-derived cellular distributions and candidate-gene associations in colorectal tumors. (A) Spatial distributions of myeloid, stromal and epithelial relative weights across sections C1–C4. Full-mode RCTD weights were normalized within each spot; myeloid and stromal subtypes were summed according to the single-cell reference annotations. Maps use a fixed 0–1 scale and H&E backgrounds displayed at 30% image intensity. Scale bars, 500 μm. (B) Total-count-adjusted rank correlations between candidate-gene expression and relative cell-type weights, calculated separately for each section. (C) Spearman correlations between relative weights and corresponding marker-expression scores. Numbers in B and C indicate correlation coefficients; color scales range from −1 to 1 and 0 to 1, respectively. Marker scores are the mean log-normalized expression of EPCAM/KRT8/KRT18 (epithelial), COL1A1/COL1A2/DCN/LUM (stromal), LST1/TYROBP/FCER1G/CTSS (myeloid), and ACTA2/TAGLN/CNN1 (smooth muscle).

Figure 10. Independent localization of EPB41L3 in GSE146771. (A) Expression profiles of author-annotated myeloid subtypes in tumor samples. Dot size indicates the patient-equal mean detection fraction, and color indicates patient-equal mean expression on the deposited scale. Only patient–subtype groups containing at least 20 cells contribute; eligible patient numbers vary by subtype and are provided in the accompanying tables. (B) EPB41L3 detection by patient and subtype. Orange and gray indicate groups with at least 20 and fewer than 20 cells, respectively. Dot size represents detection fraction; absent or zero-sized dots should be distinguished using the accompanying cell-count table. (C) Within-patient EPB41L3 detection in SPP1 TAMs and pooled other macrophages, comprising NLRP3, PLTP, IL1B and C1QC subtypes. Lines connect the same patient; both groups contain at least 20 cells. (D) Tumor SPP1 TAM counts per patient; the dashed line marks 20 cells. Analyses use the 10x cohort and original author labels.

Figure 11. Cross-cohort associations between EPB41L3 and microenvironment scores. (A) Spearman correlations with MCP-counter monocytic-lineage, fibroblast and endothelial scores in TCGA (n = 380), GSE44076 (n = 98) and GSE20916 (n = 36). Bars indicate 95% percentile confidence intervals from 2,000 bootstrap resamples. (B) Within-cohort rank plots; points represent tumor samples and lines show linear fits to ranks. Nine primary tests were adjusted jointly using the Benjamini–Hochberg method. Scores were calculated separately within each cohort.

Figure 12. Exploratory survival associations of continuous EPB41L3 expression. Hazard ratios per SD and 95% confidence intervals are shown for OS and PFI. Adjusted models include age, sex, tumor site and pathological stage. Stage-stratified models replace the stage coefficient with stage-specific baseline hazards. Microenvironment-adjusted models additionally include monocytic-lineage, fibroblast and endothelial scores. The dashed line indicates HR = 1.

Figure 13. Nonlinear associations of EPB41L3 with OS and PFI. Curves show hazard ratios relative to median expression from three-degree-of-freedom natural cubic spline models adjusted for age, sex, tumor site and stage. Shading indicates pointwise 95% confidence intervals. The displayed range spans the 1st–99th expression percentiles; models use all eligible complete cases. Overall and nonlinearity P values are from likelihood-ratio tests. OS: n = 354, 78 events; PFI: n = 352, 97 events.
